skill.name: frontend-css
skill.description: Write and maintain CSS using consistent methodology (Tailwind, BEM, CSS Modules), design tokens, framework patterns, and optimized production builds. Use this skill when writing or modifying CSS files, applying utility classes, styling components, creating design systems, defining color/spacing tokens, or working with CSS frameworks. Apply when working with .css, .scss, .sass files, Tailwind config, styled-components, CSS-in-JS, or any styling code that controls visual presentation, layout, typography, and design consistency across the application.
skill.summary: Guide consistent frontend CSS work across utilities, modules, tokens, layouts, and production optimization.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

content.value_statement: Frontend teams often mix styling methods and lose design consistency. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through CSS standards and component styling choices.
actual_capabilities: Guides work on CSS, SCSS, SASS, Less, and styling files.
Supports Tailwind utility class use and framework configuration guidance.
Applies CSS Modules, styled-components, and CSS-in-JS patterns.
Helps define colors, spacing, typography, shadows, and other design tokens.
Advises on grids, flexbox layouts, animations, transitions, and visual effects.
Encourages production CSS optimization, including removal of unused styles.
limitations: The referenced detailed standard is outside the skill package.
It provides guidance only and does not include runnable tooling.
It does not replace project-specific design system documentation.
It cannot verify visual results without a running application or screenshots.

use_cases.title: Align Component Styling
use_cases.description: Apply consistent CSS methodology when building or updating application components.

use_cases.title: Maintain Design Tokens
use_cases.description: Define and update shared colors, spacing, typography, and shadow tokens across a project.

use_cases.title: Review Styling Changes
use_cases.description: Check proposed styling work for framework fit, responsive behavior, and production readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Styling Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component styling task and recommend the best method among Tailwind, CSS Modules, BEM, or CSS-in-JS. Explain the tradeoffs briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Component Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the styling for this component using the project conventions. Keep layout, typography, spacing, and responsive behavior consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Create Design Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a token plan for colors, spacing, typography, and shadows based on the current UI. Identify naming patterns and migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit CSS Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the frontend CSS architecture for consistency, duplication, specificity issues, framework misuse, and production optimization gaps. Prioritize actionable fixes.

output_examples.input: A React component has inline styling, repeated spacing values, and inconsistent responsive behavior.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the project styling method, recommends token-backed spacing, moves repeated values into shared styles, and lists responsive breakpoints to verify.

output_examples.input: A team wants to add Tailwind classes to a shared button component.
output_examples.output: The response proposes a small variant structure, maps states to existing design tokens, and notes accessibility states that need visual coverage.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a CSS change is ready for production.
output: Checks methodology consistency and selector scope.
Reviews layout behavior across target viewports.
Flags unused styles, excessive overrides, and missing token usage.

best_practices: Keep styling choices aligned with the existing project methodology before adding new patterns.
Use design tokens for repeated colors, spacing, typography, and shadows.
Verify responsive states and production CSS cleanup before completing changes.
anti_patterns: Do not mix Tailwind, BEM, CSS Modules, and CSS-in-JS without a clear project rule.
Do not hardcode repeated visual values when shared tokens already exist.
Do not add broad overrides that depend on fragile selector specificity.

faq.question: What styling systems does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers Tailwind CSS, BEM, CSS Modules, styled-components, CSS-in-JS, and common stylesheet formats.

faq.question: Can it create a full design system?
faq.answer: It can guide token structure and styling conventions, but it does not replace product design decisions.

faq.question: Does it modify files by itself?
faq.answer: The skill provides instructions to the coding agent. File edits depend on the agent task and workspace permissions.

faq.question: Can it review existing CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help review methodology, selector scope, responsive behavior, token usage, and production cleanup.

faq.question: Does it require Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: No. Tailwind is one supported option, alongside stylesheet and component-scoped styling methods.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: The external parent-directory standards link should be replaced with bundled local guidance.
